The agent did nothing unreasonable — nothing in any tool description says the memory survives only until the next write — and it recovered in one step by copying the short scalar the listing had shown, then defensively re-ordered the rest of the run into read-all-then-write-literals. The bounded cost here (one errored round trip, 150 bytes) hides an unbounded one: had the invalidated path been /$allOf-0/datasets/0, whose value is a 4213-char object shown by title alone, there would have been no literal to copy and the remote-backed search would have had to be repeated.
